To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a ternary complex formed between a proteoglycan fragment containing G1 (binding region), link protein (L1) and a small hyaluronan (HA34) oligosaccharide has a radius of gyration (RG) not exceeding 5 nm and a cross-sectional radius of 2.0 nm.
the binding region and link-protein domains are arranged side-by-side in the ternary complex.
the binding region of the proteogrycan monomer and link protein form a compact ternary complex in solution with hyaluronan that is stabilized by side-by-side associations of the two proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of the proteogylcan aggregates in the extracellular matrix of cartilage and other connective tissues.
the structure of the ternary-complex formed between binding region, link protein (LP) and HA.
the structural organization of the ternary complexes between the G1 proteoglycan domain and link protein and with hyaluronan of different molecular weights.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of HA34 to the ternary complex of binding region and link proteins results in a more compact complex.
a ternary complex was formed between binding region, link protein, and HA450, but the precise structure could not be determined from the scattering data alone.
, although the binding region-link protein interaction is weak, it is sufficient to form a stable ternary complex with a compact structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding region and link-protein complex is compact and that this compactness does not appear to be affected by the addition of hyaluronan.
the binding region and link-protein molecules associate side-by-side in the presence of hyaluronan.

the G1 domain of proteoglycans binds to hyaluronan in the same manner as does the G1 domain to link protein and, therefore, that the ternary complex can be viewed as a dimer of G1 domains bound to the same hyaluronan chain, with a link protein sandwiched between them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding region-link protein interaction is a side-by-side association.
a small region of the proteogylcan-binding region, which contains a single immunoglobulin domain, is sufficient to bind to hyaluronan and link protein to form a ternary complex.
the ternary-complex model is consistent with the scattering data.
